column13: CORRECTED 2026-08-13. The cell previously read: say plainly that LCPcertified at $12 per report is cheaper for them, followed by a three-word causal clause asserting that the comparison is simply true - and called that the single most credible sentence on the site. The vendor page does not establish it. On lcptracker.com/solutions/lcpcertified/ (read 2026-08-13) $12 Per Report is the FIRST LINE ITEM INSIDE THE PLUS PACKAGE, immediately above Up to 5 Active Projects: $145/Month; it is not established as a standalone no-subscription option, and the Professional package ends in Contact us for Unlimited Project Pricing. If $12 per report requires the Plus subscription, a single-project weekly filer pays roughly $145/mo plus $12 per report, about $1,740 a year, against Ratepin Solo at $1,188 a year - and the referral is backwards. The sanctioned sentence quotes and declines to conclude: LCPtracker publishes LCPcertified at $12 per report and $145/month for up to 5 active projects (lcptracker.com, read 2026-08-13). If you file for one project in one county, price both before you buy here. The causal clause is deleted, not softened. BRAND.md section 3.6 and CORRECTIONS.md X-4 both require a competitor price quoted verbatim with its date and never characterised into a conclusion; X-4 struck a false claim about a competitor price that flattered us, and this was the same epistemic error flattering them. The strategic point survives intact: disqualifying the wrong buyer before they pay protects the refund rate and therefore A6. crm.competitor.diff (NOT BUILT) is specified to hash-diff this page weekly so the quotation rots loudly rather than quietly; until it exists, the read date is the only guard and the sentence must not be printed without it
